commands.name: author-cross-harness-plugins
commands.description: Creates or migrates one-source plugins that load in both Claude Code and Codex, preserving skills, agents, commands, hooks, MCP wiring, scripts, and package metadata through shared cores and thin host adapters. Use when the user asks to build, port, package, audit, or repair a plugin for both harnesses. NOT for a plugin intentionally targeting only one harness. (user)

commands.name: checks-that-bite
commands.description: Makes a check actually discriminate — tests, negative controls, guard greps, gates — and audits prose claims with the same rigor. Use when writing a negative control, reviewing assertions, or asking "is this test actually testing anything", "prove the gate bites", "the test passes but the feature is broken", "vacuous test", "red-then-green", "why didn't this catch it". Carries the vacuous-predicate bestiary (grep -q on a missing path, always-true typeof/computed-style predicates, exit-code-only asserts) and the independence law for a second derivation. NOT for choosing WHAT to test (the owning test-plan skill); NOT for triaging whether a red is contention or a real regression (flaky-gates). (user)

commands.name: closed-loop-run
commands.description: Run bounded, evidence-driven verification, diagnosis, repair, and learning cycles for any agentic task without collapsing into an unbounded recursive solver. Use when an agent must test or inspect work, identify failures, improvise locally through limited trial-and-error, progressively verify fixes, stop or escalate predictably, and produce a durable report that improves future runs. (user)

commands.name: flaky-gates
commands.description: Decides whether a RED test gate can be trusted on a host running concurrent agents and builds: reap orphaned browser/compiler processes first, then separate contention from regression with red-under-load vs green-in-isolation. Use when the tests are flaky, red in CI but green locally, a different set of tests fails every run, the suite went slow or started timing out, load average is huge, or someone asks "can I trust this red". NOT for fixing a test that fails in isolation too (the seat that owns the code); NOT for port-squatting dev servers (port-zombie-sweep owns PORT squatters, this owns CPU zombies). (user)

commands.name: generative-systems
commands.description: Analyze, design, review, or extend generative AI and generative UI systems from a harness and context-engineering perspective. Use when reasoning about manifests, registries, ontologies, schemas, skills, agents, context routing, UI IRs, renderers, validation, memory, orchestration, or portable cross-harness system architecture. (user)

commands.name: git-bare-repo-setup
commands.description: Set up, operate, and migrate to a bare-clone + sibling-worktrees local dev layout (git clone --bare, one worktree per branch, no privileged "main checkout"). Use when creating a bare layout for a repo, adding/removing branch worktrees, migrating an existing normal clone, or diagnosing tooling that breaks under the layout (branch -d refusals, lockfile/bootstrap assumptions, path-detection in scripts). Carries the gen-ui-kit reference implementation (LLD-0015) and its learned pitfalls. (user)

commands.name: i-have-adhd
commands.description: Shape output for a reader with ADHD: lead with the next action, number multi-step work, restate state across turns, suppress tangents, give specific time estimates, make wins visible. Invoke with /i-have-adhd; stays on until "stop adhd mode". (user)

commands.name: icm-architect
commands.description: Design any process, idea, problem, or body of knowledge into an ICM (Interpretable Context Methodology) workspace — folder structure as agent architecture — or restructure an existing folder, repo, or vault into one. Use when the user wants to (1) turn a recurring workflow into an agent-runnable folder pipeline, (2) organize scattered notes, files, or knowledge into a library one AI agent can walk, (3) map a team or company as connected context ("context map", "second brain", "team brain", "knowledge base for AI"), (4) audit a codebase or mixed folder into a walkable edit map (objects, processes, change-impact) so later agents can change it without slurping the tree, (5) audit or restructure an existing workspace to ICM conventions, or (6) says "make this an ICM", "ICM this", "map this repo", "audit this folder", "what would a change hit", "build me a workspace", or "structure this for agents". (user)

commands.name: import-to-claude-code
commands.description: Finish importing leftover config that `claude import` couldn't map automatically. (user)

commands.name: make-figma-agent-connector
commands.description: Brings up the local figma-bridge (tools/figma-bridge) end to end and hands back the exact values for Figma's custom MCP connector form: starts the mkcert-TLS server and an ngrok tunnel (reusing either if already live), prints the MCP server URL with its /mcp suffix and the Authorization value with its Bearer prefix, then subscribes the current session to the bridge's /events feed. Asks for nothing unless ngrok has no account configured. (user)

commands.name: port-zombie-sweep
commands.description: Finds port-squatting dev servers (vite, next, node, workerd, python http.server, and similar) that outlived the session, worktree, or agent run that started them, and suggests which to kill, grouped by project. Use when a port is "already in use", a dev server picks a random port, --strictPort fails, someone asks "what is on port 5173", "kill my stale dev servers", "port zombies", or after a batch of agent worktrees finished. Suggests only; kills nothing without the user's pick. NOT for CPU-hogging orphan browsers or compilers that hold no port (flaky-gates owns those). (user)

commands.name: progressive-context
commands.description: Design, review, or refactor universal progressive-context systems for CLI tools, AI harnesses, agents, repositories, document corpora, knowledge bases, workspaces, and folder-based systems. Use when organizing knowledge so any compatible runtime can discover the right context progressively without loading the entire corpus. (user)

commands.name: rag-board
commands.description: The Conductor's status to the human: one RAG board table (Task, Description, Status, %) printed by scripts/ragboard.py render, never composed by hand. Use for any status ask ("status?", "where are we", "show me the board", "what is running", "give me a status update") and at every natural pause: after a dispatch, after a peer report, before waiting. NOT for the board file .sdlc/board.md (Orchestrator, status-style); NOT for verdict or handoff shapes (status-style); NOT for a plan's % progress table (plan-rules). (user)

commands.name: system-atlas
commands.description: Draws a whole system as large workflow diagrams from two directions and publishes them as one full-width artifact: an inventory of its machinery (skills, agents, commands, rules, hooks, checkers, evaluators, verifiers, ontologies, knowledge bases), a machinery map, journey marks, an enforcement matrix saying which rules are actually enforced, and findings. Use when asked to map, diagram, atlas or explain how a repo, plugin, pipeline or agent system works, when onboarding onto an unfamiliar codebase, or when auditing whether the rules a project states are enforced anywhere. NOT a file-tree or dependency-graph diagram; NOT prose architecture docs; NOT a design-system page (it carries its own visual contract in DESIGN.md). (user)

commands.name: unslop
commands.description: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply. (user)

commands.name: wireframe-review
commands.description: Create and revise interactive wireframes with meaningful alternatives, on-page annotations, mixed selections and portable JSON feedback. Use for websites and application UI, not ordinary static mockups or code review. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: sdlc-lite:agent
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Launch an SDLC Lite agent by name on instructions: solo delivers a ticket, scout, researcher, architect, and archaeologist answer a question. Other names point to their own skill. NOT for creating agents.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:architect
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Design how a goal fits the existing system: approach, interfaces, constraints, rejected alternatives. Use before /plan for cross-cutting or unfamiliar work.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:ask
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Sweep the thread, task folder, tickets, run results, and notes for open questions and blockers, then ask them in one AskUserQuestion round with reasoned options, and take prose input when an answer needs it. Use for "what is still open", "what is blocking us", "ask me what you need", or before a long unattended run. NOT for guessing at questions nobody raised.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:bench
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Benchmark the agent team: run each saved task through /chain in a throwaway worktree, grade it with the real solution's hidden tests, and compare pass rate, cost, and attempts across runs. Use after changing a role, a level table, or a rubric.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:board
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) The status board for sdlc work: one table (Task, Step, Status, %) rendered from .sdlc/ by scripts/board.py, never written by hand; gains optional ID and Ticket columns when a rendered task's handoff.md has ticket front matter. Use for any status ask ("status?", "where are we", "show the board", "what is running") and at every natural pause in /chain or /bench.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:build
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Build one plan step: dispatch a builder sub-agent at a fixed model and effort per level (L1..L5). If no level is given, take it from the handoff or assess the step first. Args: [level] <step handoff.md>.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:chain
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Drive one task through the whole loop: optional scout, research, and architect, then plan, then build and verify each step with escalation, then finish loose ends, file, and close out in one question round. Use when a task should run end to end.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:checking-rules
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Discipline for a verifier checking a builder's step against its acceptance criteria: a dismissal costs the same evidence as a confirmation, a builder's "done" claim is checked against the artifact rather than trusted, and every fail reason is steelmanned before it is filed. Use when verifying a built step, clearing or dismissing a concern, or confirming a claim in a builder summary.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:checks-that-bite
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Makes a check actually discriminate — tests, negative controls, guard greps, gates — and audits prose claims with the same rigor. Use when writing a negative control, reviewing assertions, or asking "is this test actually testing anything", "prove the gate bites", "the test passes but the feature is broken", "vacuous test", "red-then-green", "why didn't this catch it". Carries the vacuous-predicate bestiary (grep -q on a missing path, always-true typeof/computed-style predicates, exit-code-only asserts) and the independence law for a second derivation. NOT for choosing WHAT to test (the owning test-plan skill); NOT for triaging whether a red is contention or a real regression (flaky-gates).

commands.name: sdlc-lite:clarify
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Sharpen a vague or overloaded ask into an executable one (root goal, deltas, scoped do with a done-condition) and write it into the task handoff. An ask that already states its scope and done-condition passes through in one line. Use for "what are they actually asking for", "is this ask scoped", or before /plan on a fuzzy request. NOT for a greenfield design with most decisions unmade (/grill); NOT for splitting scoped work into parts (/decompose).

commands.name: sdlc-lite:decompose
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Break a scoped problem into parts along two independent planes, outside-in (whole to parts, the structure) and inside-out (actions to surfaces, the behavior), then prove they cover each other with scripts/coverage_check.py. Use when breaking down a technical or UX architecture, a goal, or a system; when a breakdown has structure with no behavior; or when acceptance criteria map to no task. NOT for greenfield decisions still unmade (/grill first); NOT for a concrete screen layout.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:dig
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Explain why code is the way it is: history, decisions, landmines, from git history.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:fanout
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Run ticket lanes in parallel: each lane is a git worktree whose tickets run one at a time through the lane `steps.py lane` picks (the `solo` agent for ticket levels L1 and L2, the headless /chain for the rest), merge into an integration branch behind gates, and close there. On the Claude host the parent can dispatch the lanes as isolated background sub-agents (`fanout.py prep` and `land`). Use when several ready tickets can run side by side.
commands.argumentHint: <lane>=<ids>... <lane>@<branch>=<ids>... [--base REF] [--integration BRANCH] [--gate CMD]... [--lanes-dir DIR] [--rewrite-refs] [--lane auto|solo|full] [--max-lanes N] [--stagger SECS]

commands.name: sdlc-lite:file
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Draft the records for a finished task (PR title and body, changelog entry, follow-ups) from its .sdlc artifacts, then publish only what the user approves.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:fix
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Fast lane for a ticket level L1 item (a doc line, a lint tweak, one test, a one-file fix), run only when the user asks for /fix or the lane script prints `fix`; ticket levels L1 and L2 go to the `solo` agent by default. The conductor writes the step handoff itself, runs builder L1 or L2 and verifier L1, and closes the ticket inline with `tickets.py close --reason`; no planner, no filer, no follow-up tickets. Use for "/fix" by name. NOT for a level L1 or L2 ticket by default, which goes to solo; NOT for work touching more than one file's behavior or needing a plan, which is /chain.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:fleet-retro
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Run a retro of how SDLC Lite served several repos at once: collect each repo's fingerprint, detect waste and stalls mechanically, interview each repo's conductor, write one cost-ranked report where every finding carries an evidence pointer and [V] or [U], check the findings with a sampled verifier and the actionability rubric, and file the confirmed ones after one approval round. Use for "retro across my repos", "where is the plugin costing us", or a periodic fleet review. NOT for one repo's run traces (review-traces), a live status view (board), or unattended filing.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:fleet-status
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) The status of every active repo in one screen, in a fixed order: machine load with a verdict, what needs the user, what is really moving, what is stale or stuck, what finished since the last report, and release state. Printed by scripts/fleet_status.py render, never composed by hand, then at most one AskUserQuestion round for the Needs-you items. Use for "fleet status", "status across repos", "what needs me", "what is stuck", "what is running everywhere". NOT for one repo's task table (/board); NOT for messaging conductors.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:grill
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Derive the load-bearing design decisions for a greenfield system, component family, or feature whose decision space is mostly unmade, in grounded, cascading AskUserQuestion rounds until it settles, then write the ratified design to the task. Use for "grill me on the design", "nothing is decided yet", "what do we need to decide". NOT for sharpening one given ask (/clarify); NOT for splitting settled work into parts (/decompose).

commands.name: sdlc-lite:handoff
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Start an sdlc task: create .sdlc/<task>/handoff.md from the current discussion so clean-context agents get everything they need.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:onboard
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Set up or check the entry files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) and the docs layout for a repository adopting SDLC Lite, keeping anything the repository already wrote. NOT for moving existing documents into the layout.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:open-questions
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Clear a task's unresolved items (open questions, unconfirmed defaults, undecided choices) in one batched AskUserQuestion round at the end of a /chain run or session. Use for "anything still open", "loose ends", "close this out", or "what's still pending". NOT for ambiguity before a task starts (/clarify); NOT for filing new work as tickets (/ticket).

commands.name: sdlc-lite:plan
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Plan a task: dispatch the planner to produce ordered steps with acceptance criteria and a builder level per step. Use when a goal is ready to be broken into buildable steps.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:plan-campaign
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Plan a wave-based campaign (build the tool and gate, migrate N units in parallel lanes, bulk review, bulk PRs) and return one /goal block plus a lane partition. Use for "migrate every page", "plan a campaign", or a standard that must hold across many units. NOT for a single goal (plan-goal), one fanout run (plan-fanout), or running anything.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:plan-doc
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Write a plan doc: one file with the goal, outcome block, measures, authorization, stop rules and ordered ticket steps with runnable criteria, linted by plan_check.py plan, so a smaller session can run it with run-plan. Use for "write a plan doc", "plan this so a smaller model can run it", or before /goal complete build and verify <plan-doc.md>. NOT for a goal with no steps to keep (plan-goal), for running a plan doc (run-plan), or for one step's builder handoff (plan).

commands.name: sdlc-lite:plan-fanout
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Plan a fanout run: choose ready tickets, group them into lanes with no file overlap, set the lane cap, stagger, gate, and budget, check the command with plan_check.py and fanout.py --dry-run, and return one copy/paste fanout command. Use for "run these tickets in parallel" or "plan a fanout". NOT for running it.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:plan-goal
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Plan a /goal session: gather the scope and limits from the thread and repo, apply the goal rules (a checkable done-when, stop rules with numbers, explicit authorization), check the block with plan_check.py, and return one copy/paste /goal block. Use for "write me a goal", "overnight goal", or before unattended work. NOT for running the goal.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:plan-loop
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Plan a /loop: pick the interval or dynamic mode, write a self-contained idempotent prompt with a stop condition, check it with plan_check.py, and return one copy/paste /loop line. Use for "check this every 20 minutes", "keep watching X", or a status loop. NOT for running the loop.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:plan-verification
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Capture the outcome a plan serves: one outcome sentence with its why, a measure with its before value and target, a 3 to 5 criterion rubric, and a negative control, as lines another plan skill places in its block. Use before a goal is written (plan-goal reads it), or for "what is this goal for", "how will we know it worked", "add a measure to this goal". NOT for step criteria (planner), pass or fail on built work (verifier), or creating a goal or KPI file.
commands.argumentHint: [goal id such as G-001, or the outcome in a sentence]

commands.name: sdlc-lite:research
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Research an outside-world question (docs, APIs, libraries) with cited findings.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:review-traces
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Review a project's sdlc run traces for waste and bugs caused by sdlc-lite, with no model call in the ingest and detect stages, then diagnose, verify, propose, and file each confirmed finding as a ticket after approval.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:run-plan
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Run an approved plan doc to completion unattended: preflight, then loop plan_done.py, dispatch each open step through fanout.py prep and land, follow steps.py next, and stop with state written when a script says stop. Built for a smaller driver model that follows exit codes and carries no judgment. Use for "/goal complete build and verify <plan-doc.md>" or "run this plan doc". NOT for writing the plan (plan-doc), a goal with no plan doc (plan-goal), or one ticket (solo).

commands.name: sdlc-lite:scout
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Map where the code for a question lives: files, symbols, entry points. Fast and read-only.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:sdlc-lite
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Run SDLC Lite workflows in Codex: tickets, handoffs, plans, builds, verification, chains, boards, and parallel lanes. Use for structured software delivery or SDLC Lite status. Includes native Codex role execution and project-scoped predefined subagents. Requires authenticated Codex CLI for pipeline roles.

commands.name: sdlc-lite:ticket
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Stamp a typed ticket with the next id, or generate the roadmap (.sdlc/roadmap.md, or .sdlc/tickets/roadmap.md with layout: topics) from ticket front matter in dependency order. NOT for free-text briefs, which stay with /handoff.
commands.argumentHint: new <type> <slug> "title" [--numbered] | close <slug> [--force] [--reason "<text>"] [--ack-warnings "<why>"] [--dry-run] [--skip N[,N...]] [--ticket N] [--expect DIGEST] [--numbered] | roadmap [--numbered] | check [--numbered] | archive [--dry-run] [--rewrite-refs] [--force] [--numbered] | number [--dry-run] | migrate-layout [--dry-run] [--rewrite-refs]

commands.name: sdlc-lite:verify
commands.description: (sdlc-lite) Verify a built step: dispatch the independent verifier against the step's acceptance criteria. Use after /build.

commands.name: progressive-context:progressive-context
commands.description: (progressive-context) Organize a project's context through small entry points and linked capability contracts. Use to capture an intended component or capability, assess its implementation against intent, prepare it for reuse, or repair bloated context navigation. Supports code, UI, research, content, and process projects. Not for executing a ticket plan or claiming tests passed without evidence.

commands.name: figma:figma-code-connect
commands.description: (Figma) Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.

commands.name: figma:figma-create-new-file
commands.description: (Figma) Always use this skill when the user wants to create a new Figma Design, FigJam, or Slides file. You MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call.

commands.name: figma:figma-design-to-code
commands.description: (Figma) **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.

commands.name: figma:figma-generate-design
commands.description: (Figma) Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.

commands.name: figma:figma-generate-diagram
commands.description: (Figma) MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).

commands.name: figma:figma-generate-library
commands.description: (Figma) Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.

commands.name: figma:figma-generative-plugins
commands.description: (Figma) **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_generative_plugin` or `update_generative_plugin`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or extend a reusable generative Figma plugin.

commands.name: figma:figma-implement-motion
commands.description: (Figma) Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.

commands.name: figma:figma-shaders
commands.description: (Figma) **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_shader` or `update_shader`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or iterate on a shader effect, shader fill, custom effect, custom fill, or procedural shader in Figma.

commands.name: figma:figma-swiftui
commands.description: (Figma) SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.

commands.name: figma:figma-use
commands.description: (Figma) **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

commands.name: figma:figma-use-figjam
commands.description: (Figma) This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the FigJam context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.

commands.name: figma:figma-use-motion
commands.description: (Figma) Motion / animation context for the `use_figma` MCP tool — animating Figma nodes via manual keyframes, animation styles, easing, and timeline duration. Load alongside figma-use whenever a task involves adding, editing, or inspecting animation on a node.

commands.name: figma:figma-use-slides
commands.description: (Figma) This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.

commands.name: figma-suite:figma-suite
commands.description: (figma-suite) Bidirectional design system sync between code and Figma — tokens/variables, components, and a Zod-validated code<->Figma component mapping — plus component library generation, screen design composition, and design audit. Use when syncing design tokens or components to/from Figma, keeping code and Figma components in sync, mapping code props to Figma properties (incl. Code Connect), building Figma component libraries, designing new screens in Figma, or auditing Figma files for compliance.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)
